critical_findings.finding: Sensitive/private information can be unintentionally published because the product outputs a static site with no access control (explicit non-goal) and the current plan accepts K8 with documentation-only mitigation; this can still fail in practice if users deploy to a public host without realizing exposure scope (including search index artifacts which can make extraction easier).

closure.closure_target: Risk K8 must have an explicit acceptance statement AND concrete user-facing safeguards documented (minimum: pre-build checklist + explicit deploy-risk acknowledgment + output inventory/report that enumerates included notes and emitted index artifacts).

critical_findings.finding: Actual note-set scale is a blocking unknown (Q3). If the real corpus exceeds the assumed ~1,000 notes or includes large files, the monolithic in-memory pipeline can become slow or crash/hang (K4), causing inability to build/publish and potential data loss if outputs are partially written.

closure.closure_target: Confirm Q3 with an explicit upper-bound target; add build-time resource budgets (time/memory) and a fail-fast/partial-output safety strategy (write to temp dir then atomic swap).

closure.mitigation_plan: Add scale confirmation gate; implement progress logging + cancellation; avoid unbounded memory growth (cap caches, avoid storing duplicate representations); ensure output emission is transactional to prevent corrupted/partial sites.

critical_findings.finding: XSS/content injection can occur if Markdown rendering allows raw HTML or templates fail to escape user-controlled strings (title, tags, link text). Even in a trusted-user environment, sharing the generated site (or opening locally) can execute malicious payloads from imported notes, copied snippets, or third-party content; additionally, search index content rendered into DOM can become an injection vector.

closure.closure_target: Implement security-by-default rendering: sanitize/disable raw HTML in Markdown by default; escape all template variables; ensure search UI safely renders snippets (textContent, not innerHTML); add XSS fixture tests.

critical_findings.finding: Internal link and backlink correctness can fail due to ambiguous conventions (Q1), inconsistent resolver precedence, anchors/fragments, and slug/title collisions; this can produce broken navigation, incorrect backlink lists, or silent mislinks (high trust impact).

closure.closure_target: Define a deterministic link resolution algorithm with explicit precedence (path-based canonical IDs), collision detection with actionable errors/warnings, and fixture-based tests covering Q1 scenarios; ensure broken links are surfaced consistently (R18).

critical_findings.finding: Generated links/assets can break when hosted under a subdirectory (e.g., GitHub Pages project sites) or when viewed via file:// due to incorrect base URL assumptions and absolute vs relative URL generation. This can break navigation, search index loading, and CSS/JS assets.

closure.closure_target: Implement and test basePath/baseUrl handling end-to-end (pages, assets, search index fetch paths, internal links) with a deployment matrix; ensure default output uses robust relative URLs where possible.

closure.closure_target: Choose and document the search approach with explicit budgets (index size, load time, query latency) and build-time reporting; add relevance acceptance fixtures (expected top results) and performance tests at the confirmed scale.

critical_findings.finding: Build may fail or generate broken links on Windows/macOS/Linux due to path separator differences, case sensitivity, reserved filenames, Unicode normalization differences, and non-UTF8 file encodings; this can also corrupt slug generation and link resolution.

closure.closure_target: Define and implement canonical path normalization + encoding handling rules; add cross-platform test fixtures and explicit error/warn behavior for unreadable or non-UTF8 files; ensure slug generation is stable across OSes.

closure.mitigation_plan: Normalize to POSIX-like internal paths; treat file path as the canonical ID; use robust Unicode handling; provide a skip-with-report option for problematic files.

critical_findings.finding: Non-deterministic build outputs (unordered file discovery, tag ordering, locale/timezone effects) can cause noisy diffs and unreliable deployments, making it hard to verify that changes are intentional and increasing regression risk.

closure.closure_target: Guarantee deterministic ordering (sorted paths, stable tag/link ordering) and avoid timestamps/non-deterministic identifiers in outputs by default; add a repeat-build equivalence check in CI/QA.

critical_findings.finding: A user, misunderstanding the public nature of static site hosting, deploys the generated site, inadvertently making private notes (e.g., containing passwords, personal data) publicly accessible. Since access control is a non-goal, the tool does not prevent this leakage.

closure.rationale: Per DEC6, access control is an explicit non-goal. The risk is accepted with documentation-only mitigation, consisting of a README disclaimer and a build-time warning banner, planned for M5 (DL25).

critical_findings.finding: A user includes untrusted content (e.g., copy-pasted from a website) in a Markdown note. If the build process renders raw HTML without sanitization, malicious scripts can execute in the context of the generated site, leading to potential data theft or other client-side attacks.

closure.mitigation_plan: Per DEC7, the Markdown renderer will sanitize all HTML input by default to prevent injection attacks. This is scheduled for implementation in M5 (DL24).

critical_findings.finding: As the number of notes grows towards the target scale (1,000+ notes), the client-side search index becomes excessively large, leading to slow page load times and unresponsive search UI in the browser, rendering a core feature unusable.

closure.mitigation_plan: Per K5 mitigation strategy, the system will be designed with an indexing approach appropriate for the scale target (R22), with performance validated in M4.

critical_findings.finding: The build process generates identical output paths for different source notes (e.g., `folder1/topic.md` and `folder2/topic.md` both becoming `topic.html`), causing one note's content to be silently overwritten. The final site is missing content without any build error.

closure.mitigation_plan: Per K10 mitigation, the build process must implement collision detection for output paths, failing the build or using a deterministic deduplication strategy. This is part of graph consistency checks planned in M3 (DL13).

critical_findings.finding: A user's notes contain a mix of internal link formats (e.g., standard relative links and wiki-links). The build process, configured for only one format, silently ignores the others, resulting in a partially broken site with missing links and incomplete backlink data.

closure.mitigation_plan: Per K2 mitigation, provide configurable link parsing (R15). Additionally, per R18, the system will emit build-time warnings for all unresolved links to alert the user to potential issues.

critical_findings.finding: The build process relies on OS-specific path conventions (e.g., hardcoded '/' separators). When a user runs the tool on a different OS (e.g., Windows), the build fails during file discovery or link resolution, making the tool unusable outside its development environment.

closure.mitigation_plan: Per K11 mitigation, the build pipeline must use OS-agnostic path handling libraries and be tested across Windows, macOS, and Linux via automated CI to ensure portability.
